Finally he specifies a holy incense of sweet spices, gum resin, onycha, galbanum and frankincense, and forbids making either the oil or the incense for ordinary use, on penalty of being cut off from the people.

The LORD instructs Moses on the incense altar, the census ransom, the bronze basin, the holy anointing oil, and the holy incense. He declares the altar most holy, promises to meet Moses before the covenant, and threatens that those who copy the oil or incense or put the oil on a stranger will be cut off from their people.

Moses receives the LORD's instructions in several speeches: to make the incense altar, collect the atonement money, make the basin, compound the anointing oil, and prepare the incense. He is told to anoint the Tent of Meeting, its furnishings, and Aaron and his sons, and to speak to the children of Israel about the oil.

Aaron is to burn incense on the altar every morning when he tends the lamps and at evening when he lights them. He is to make atonement on the altar's horns once a year with sin offering blood. He and his sons must wash their hands and feet at the basin so they do not die, and they are to be anointed and sanctified to serve as priests.

The children of Israel are to give a half-shekel ransom for each person aged twenty and over when counted, with rich and poor giving the same, to avoid plague. Moses is to tell them that the holy anointing oil is holy throughout their generations and must not be copied, nor the incense made for themselves.

The altar is to be made of acacia wood, a cubit square and two cubits high, with horns of one piece, overlaid with pure gold, with a gold molding, two gold rings, and gold-overlaid poles. It is placed before the veil by the ark and mercy seat, and only incense is allowed on it, with no strange incense, burnt, meal, or drink offerings. It is anointed with the holy oil and is most holy.

l: incense of sweet spices, Exodus, Chapter 30
s: Sweet incense is burned on the altar every morning and evening as a perpetual incense before the LORD. The holy incense is made from equal weights of sweet spices, gum resin, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, seasoned with salt. Some is beaten small and placed before the covenant, and anyone who makes any like it to smell it is to be cut off.

When the people are counted, each man aged twenty and up gives half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel (twenty gerahs) as a ransom for his soul, so that no plague comes. The rich do not give more or the poor less. The money is appointed for the service of the Tent of Meeting as a memorial and atonement.

The Tent of Meeting is where the basin stands between it and the altar, and where Aaron and his sons must wash before entering so they do not die. It is the first item to be anointed with the holy oil, and the atonement money is appointed for its service. Some of the incense is placed before the covenant in it, where the LORD will meet Moses.

l: basin (basin and its base), Exodus, Chapter 30
s: The basin and its base are to be made of bronze and set between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, filled with water. Aaron and his sons wash their hands and feet in it before entering the Tent or approaching the altar, as a statute forever. The basin and its base are also anointed with the holy oil.

The oil is compounded by a perfumer from 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, 250 of cinnamon, 250 of cane, 500 of cassia, and a hin of olive oil. It is used to anoint and sanctify the Tent of Meeting, the ark, the table, the lamp stand, both altars, the basin, and Aaron and his sons. It must not be poured on ordinary people or imitated, and offenders are cut off from their people.

The LORD tells Moses that he has called Bezalel, son of Uri of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the Spirit of God and skill in all kinds of craftsmanship. He appoints Oholiab, son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, to work with Bezalel, and puts wisdom in all the wise-hearted so they can make everything commanded, including the Tent of Meeting, the ark, the furniture, the priestly garments, the anointing oil and the incense. The LORD then tells Moses to instruct the children of Israel to keep his Sabbaths as a perpetual sign and covenant, on pain of death for anyone who works on that day, because he made heaven and earth in six days and rested on the seventh. When he finishes speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gives him the two stone tablets of the covenant, written with God's finger.

The LORD calls Bezalel by name, fills him with the Spirit of God, appoints Oholiab to work with him, and lists everything that is to be made for the Tent and the priesthood. He commands Moses to tell Israel to keep the Sabbath as a sign that he is the LORD who sanctifies them, and he gives Moses the two tablets of the covenant on Mount Sinai.

Moses receives the LORD's word naming Bezalel and Oholiab as craftsmen for the work. He is told to speak to the children of Israel about keeping the Sabbath, and at the end of the LORD's speech on Mount Sinai he is given the two stone tablets of the covenant.

Bezalel is the son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and the LORD calls him by name. He is filled with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge and skill in workmanship, including work in gold, silver and bronze, stone cutting and wood carving.

Oholiab, son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, is appointed by the LORD to work with Bezalel. He is mentioned alongside the other wise-hearted people in whom the LORD has put wisdom to make all that was commanded.

The Tent of Meeting is the first of the things the LORD commands to be made, along with the ark of the covenant, the mercy seat and all the furniture of the Tent. The furniture includes the table, the lamp stand, the altars, the basin and its base.

The children of Israel are to be told by Moses to keep the LORD's Sabbaths throughout their generations as a sign and a perpetual covenant. Anyone among them who works on the Sabbath is to be put to death and cut off from the people.

The Sabbath is described as a sign between the LORD and Israel forever, marking that he sanctifies them. It is a day of solemn rest, holy to the LORD, on the seventh day after six days of work, rooted in the LORD making heaven and earth in six days and resting on the seventh. Profaning it or working on it is punishable by death.

l: two tablets of the covenant, Exodus, Chapter 31
s: The LORD gives Moses the two tablets of the covenant when he finishes speaking with him on Mount Sinai. They are stone tablets written with God's finger.

When Moses delays on the mountain, the people of Israel ask Aaron to make gods, and Aaron collects their golden earrings and fashions a molded calf, proclaiming a feast to the LORD. The LORD tells Moses of their corruption and threatens to consume them, but Moses pleads, citing the Egyptians and the promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and the LORD relents. Moses comes down carrying the two tablets, sees the calf and the dancing, breaks the tablets, burns and grinds the calf and makes the people drink it, and confronts Aaron. The sons of Levi respond to Moses' call and kill about three thousand men at his command, and Moses then returns to the LORD to seek atonement, offering to be blotted out of the LORD's book. The LORD says he will blot out whoever sinned, tells Moses to lead the people on with his angel going before them, and strikes the people for what they did with the calf.

Moses is delayed on the mountain, intercedes for the people when the LORD threatens to consume them, and wins the LORD's reprieve. He descends, breaks the tablets in anger, destroys the calf, rebukes Aaron, calls for those on the LORD's side, and commands the sons of Levi to kill. He then returns to the LORD, offers to be blotted out of the book if the people are not forgiven, and is told to lead the people onward.

Aaron collects the people's golden earrings, fashions the molded calf, builds an altar before it, and proclaims a feast to the LORD. When Moses confronts him, he blames the people's evil bent and says he threw the gold into the fire and the calf came out. The text says he had let the people lose control, causing derision among their enemies, and the calf is described at the end as the one Aaron made.

The LORD tells Moses that the people have corrupted themselves and calls them stiff-necked, threatening to consume them and make a great nation of Moses. He turns away from the threatened evil after Moses' plea, but later says he will blot out whoever has sinned against him and will punish them in the day when he punishes. He directs Moses to lead the people onward with his angel going before, and he strikes the people because of the calf.

The people, seeing Moses delayed, demand gods from Aaron, give up their gold earrings, and worship the molded calf with offerings, eating, drinking, and play. Moses burns the calf, grinds it, and makes them drink it, and about three thousand of them die. Moses calls their act a great sin, and the LORD strikes them for it.

The golden calf is made by Aaron from the people's gold earrings, shaped with an engraving tool into a molded calf. The people declare it the gods who brought them out of Egypt, and offerings are made before it. Moses burns it, grinds it to powder, scatters it on the water, and makes the Israelites drink it.
All the sons of Levi gather to Moses when he calls for those on the LORD's side. They carry out his command to go through the camp with swords, and about three thousand men fall.

l: tablets of the covenant, Exodus, Chapter 32
s: The tablets are described as the work of God, written on both sides with God's own engraved writing. Moses carries them down the mountain, but in anger at seeing the calf and the dancing he throws them from his hands and breaks them beneath the mountain.

l: killing of about three thousand men, Exodus, Chapter 32
s: At Moses' word, relaying the LORD's command, the sons of Levi go from gate to gate through the camp killing brother, companion, and neighbor. About three thousand men of the people fall that day. Moses then tells the Levites to consecrate themselves to the LORD so that he may give them a blessing.

The LORD tells Moses to lead the Israelites from Horeb toward the land promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, with an angel going ahead, but says he will not go among them because they are stiff-necked. The people mourn and strip off their jewelry. Moses pitches the Tent of Meeting outside the camp, where the pillar of cloud descends and the LORD speaks with him face to face while the people worship at their tent doors. Moses pleads for the LORD's presence to go with them, and the LORD agrees. Moses then asks to see the LORD's glory, and the LORD promises to pass his goodness before him and proclaim his name, but says Moses may see only his back, hidden in a cleft of the rock, not his face.

The LORD commands Moses to lead the people to the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, promising an angel and the driving out of its peoples, but says he will not go among the stiff-necked Israelites lest he consume them. After Moses pleads, he promises that his presence will go with Moses and give him rest, and he speaks with Moses face to face as with a friend. He refuses to show his face, saying no man can see it and live, but promises to pass his goodness before Moses, proclaim his name, and let him see his back.

Moses pitches the Tent of Meeting outside the camp and enters it to speak with the LORD, who speaks with him face to face as with a friend. He asks to know whom the LORD will send and to be shown his way, insists that the LORD's presence must go with them or they should not go up, and asks to see the LORD's glory. The LORD grants the first requests, and Moses is to be placed in a cleft of the rock and covered by the LORD's hand as he passes.

The Israelites are called a stiff-necked people and hear the evil news that the LORD will not go up among them. They mourn, put on no jewelry, and strip off their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward at the LORD's command. When Moses goes to the Tent, they rise and watch him from their tent doors, and when the pillar of cloud descends they worship.

It is the land the LORD swore to give to the offspring of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, described as flowing with milk and honey. The LORD says he will send an angel ahead and drive out the Canaanite, Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite.

Moses used to pitch the tent far outside the camp and call it the Tent of Meeting, and everyone who sought the LORD went out to it. When Moses entered, the pillar of cloud stood at its door and the LORD spoke with him there. The people watched from their own tent doors and worshiped.

The pillar of cloud descends and stands at the door of the Tent of Meeting whenever Moses enters, and the LORD speaks with Moses. All the people see it and rise to worship, each at their own tent door.
